title: When AI Changes the Controls That Govern AI
subtitle: A first-party reliability case on deterministic control-plane integrity, false internal success, cost-aware recovery, and independent customer-outcome verification

customer_outcome_contract.request: A signed-in customer gives the front person a normal sentence for a named business or service.
customer_outcome_contract.accepted_effect: The app returns plain customer-facing status and an unauthenticated public page that matches the request.
rejected_substitutes: builder or verifier success without a public page
a done message whose link returns NOT_GENERATED
pipeline jargon shown as customer copy

classifications.VERIFIED_RECEIPT: A committed receipt binds a dated run, tested release and observed public effect or failure. It proves only that bounded run.
classifications.REPOSITORY_SUPPORTED: Immutable repository metadata or source supports the statement, but does not independently prove a customer outcome.
classifications.OWNER_OBSERVED: The account owner reports the production behavior. It is material testimony, not independent measurement.
classifications.UNKNOWN: The current state or quantity has not been re-proved under the stated customer contract.

claims.statement: A named-business production run returned a public HTTP 200 page headed Meridian Tax Group in 13,684 ms.
claims.scope: One named-business prompt on one dated app release.
claims.limitation: The receipt does not identify a runtime implementation SHA and does not prove other prompt classes.
claims.receipt_hash_scope: SHA-256 of the receipt payload canonicalized by the incident runner; not a digital signature or literal file-byte hash.

claims.statement: On the same dated app release, a generic trade-description run failed to publish before timing out at 302,662 ms.
claims.limitation: A later repair may change the result; no fresh production receipt is cited here.
claims.receipt_hash_scope: SHA-256 of the receipt payload canonicalized by the incident runner; not a digital signature or literal file-byte hash.

claims.statement: The 07:28 incident matrix recorded three component rows verified and one optional generic-trade row open.
claims.limitation: Only the named-entity row traversed the complete customer path. Workspace isolation and runtime readiness were component checks, so this is not a 3/3 customer-outcome pass.
Size and co-author metadata do not prove sole authorship, causation, or a universal tool ranking.

claims.statement: A later ten-scenario compile/router suite produced valid planned routes for all ten scenarios.
claims.scope: Local contract compilation and routing simulation.
claims.limitation: It did not build, publish, or fetch customer pages.

claims.statement: The subsequent ten-scenario live run recorded ten timeouts and zero delivered scenarios.
claims.scope: One expanded live run targeting the production baseline.
claims.limitation: The candidate branch was not deployed to the target host, so this proves missing end-to-end delivery on that target, not candidate quality.

claims.statement: The account owner reports a multi-day customer-impact incident, repeated premature fixed declarations, paid attempts without deliverables, and client-facing internal jargon.
claims.scope: Owner experience and production reproductions during this incident.
claims.limitation: Duration, spend and attribution are not independently quantified in this bundle.

claims.statement: Current full customer-outcome closure is unknown pending a fresh same-release run across named, generic, complex and repair scenarios.
claims.limitation: No later complete same-release production receipt is cited.

claims.statement: No controlled evidence in this case supports a universal ranking of Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, or any model.
claims.limitation: A valid ranking requires frozen tasks, equal budgets and permissions, repeated runs, independent scoring and customer-effect acceptance.

corrections.prior_claim: 25 July was the last demonstrated working run.
corrections.replacement: The record contains later bounded receipts. No single last-known-good claim is used without a complete same-release evidence chain.
corrections.reason: The prior wording collapsed different API, UI, runtime and publication proofs into one date.

corrections.prior_claim: The required customer path passed 3/3 and therefore represented current closure.
corrections.replacement: The legacy matrix recorded 3/4 component rows, while full customer-path prompt outcomes were one bounded pass and one bounded failure.
corrections.reason: The rows tested different layers and were later superseded by an expanded customer-URL gate.

corrections.replacement: 2b818e... is the tested app/static release bound to the dated receipts; runtime_source_sha was not established.
corrections.reason: A receipt-bound app release is not proof of the runtime implementation identity.

corrections.replacement: Publication source is Noetfield-Systems/Noetfield; incident implementation evidence is in Noetfield-Systems/NOETFIELD-RUNWAY.
corrections.reason: Separating publication and product repositories prevents provenance confusion.

attribution_boundary: Tool names on this page come from commit, pull-request or session metadata. Metadata can support co-authorship or assistance, but not sole authorship, intent, causation, or general tool quality.
privacy_boundary: Raw session and project identifiers are not repeated here. Stable hashes are pseudonymous and may remain linkable across disclosures; they are not anonymous.

minimum_protocol: same written task and acceptance contract
equal permissions, compute and time budget
at least three repeated runs per tool
hash-bound raw outputs and correction log

scope: One repository-scoped, multi-day Company New incident and its dated repair evidence.
proves: One named-business customer path produced a public page on a dated app release.
One generic trade-description customer path timed out on that same dated app release.
Component-level green signals did not establish the complete customer effect.
The later expanded live run did not deliver on its target.
does_not_prove: A universal ranking of Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, or any model.
Sole authorship, intent, or tool causation.
Current production recovery or generic-trade delivery.
External customer adoption, revenue, or certification.
